title: Minimised content – summary only
description: For deployments that must keep as little personal content as possible: the summary is the only record of what was said that is kept, and it is written to leave out sensitive personal information. Consent comes first: Meeting Consent mode Opt-in with the each-participant rule, a meeting may only use this mode or a stricter one, streaming clients without a consent step are refused, the Virtual Participant leaves after an objection, and evidence screenshots are kept. Stream Audio/Video and the Desktop Capture App cannot collect each participant's consent, so Start is refused from them; use a Virtual Participant on a join that supports each-participant consent (not the Webex join). Meeting audio, screen video from streaming clients and Virtual Participant meeting video are not recorded, personal information is redacted from transcripts (in en-US, en-AU, en-GB and es-US), the meeting chat is not added to the transcript, and Amazon Bedrock models run within this deployment's geography. The transcript is deleted as soon as the summary is written, and so is any recording that is still stored (an uploaded meeting's audio, for example). New meetings are summarized with the minimised-content summary profile, whose sections tell the model to leave out health and medical information and the other categories of sensitive personal information (such as religion, sexual orientation, political opinions, trade union membership, and genetic and biometric data), and Meeting Assistant › Leave out sensitive personal information is on, so the assistant is given the same rule after its instructions, whatever they say. This is an instruction to the model, not a filter: it usually leaves such information out, but it can miss some, so review summaries where that matters. A meeting whose owner chooses another summary profile, or a summary regenerated with one, does not get the instruction. The meeting assistant settings otherwise keep their shipped defaults. Some controls are stack parameters rather than settings, and have to be set when the stack is deployed or updated: EnableVideoRecording false, the deployment-wide limit no setting or launch overrides, so no meeting video from any client and no key frames are kept; TranscriptKnowledgeBase DISABLED if summaries must not be indexed for search across meetings; LogLevel INFO or WARN (DEBUG logs meeting content); and the retention periods MeetingRecordExpirationInDays, TranscriptionExpirationInDays, AudioRecordingExpirationInDays and CloudWatchLogsExpirationInDays. See "Minimised content" in docs/privacy-and-data-handling.md. Consent given in advance is allowed, for at most 365 days, and is kept without the sign-in device's details. Meetings are shared with the people on their participant list (Meeting Sharing on), who see a read-only page without the owner's own material.

values.videoNoticeText: Video of the meeting, including shared screens and any visible camera feeds, is also recorded.
